papers.title: An Accurate and Efficient Approach to Knowledge Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Structured Ontology Models, Graph Neural Networks, and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of biomedical literature makes it challenging for researchers to stay current. Integrating knowledge from various sources is crucial for studying complex biological systems. Traditional text-mining methods often have limited accuracy because they don’t capture semantic and contextual nuances. Deep-learning models can be computationally expensive and typically have low interpretability, though efforts in explainable AI aim to mitigate this. Furthermore, transformer-based models have a tendency to produce false or made-up information—a problem known as hallucination—which is especially prevalent in large language models (LLMs). This study proposes a hybrid approach combining text-mining techniques with graph neural networks (GNNs) and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) to extend biomedical knowledge graphs and interpret predicted edges based on published literature. An LLM is used to validate predictions and provide explanations. Evaluated on a corpus of experimentally confirmed protein interactions, the approach achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.772. Applied to insomnia, the approach identified 25 interactions between 32 human proteins absent in known knowledge bases, including regulatory interactions between MAOA and 5-HT2C, binding between ADAM22 and 14-3-3 proteins, which is implicated in neurological diseases, and a circadian regulatory loop involving RORB and NR1D1. The hybrid GNN-LLM method analyzes biomedical literature efficiency to uncover potential molecular interactions for complex disorders. It can accelerate therapeutic target discovery by focusing expert verification on the most relevant automatically extracted information.

papers.title: Hierarchical Attentional Hybrid Neural Networks for Document Classification
papers.abstract: Document classification is a challenging task with important applications. The deep learning approaches to the problem have gained much attention recently. Despite the progress, the proposed models do not incorporate the knowledge of the document structure in the architecture efficiently and not take into account the contexting importance of words and sentences. In this paper, we propose a new approach based on a combination of convolutional neural networks, gated recurrent units, and attention mechanisms for document classification tasks. The main contribution of this work is the use of convolution layers to extract more meaningful, generalizable and abstract features by the hierarchical representation. The proposed method in this paper improves the results of the current attention-based approaches for document classification.

papers.title: Combining machine learning, simulations and experiments for improved glass design
papers.abstract: The design of novel glasses with tailored properties remains a grand challenge in materials science, traditionally requiring extensive trial-and-error experimentation. This talk presents a comprehensive framework that integrates machine learning, atomistic simulations, and targeted experiments to accelerate the discovery and optimization of glass compositions. We demonstrate how large-scale machine learning models trained on experimental databases can predict glass properties across nearly the entire periodic table, enabling rapid screening of promising compositions. These predictions are refined through physics-informed graph neural networks that capture atomic-scale interactions and energy conservation principles, providing deeper insights into structure-property relationships. The framework is enhanced by automated knowledge extraction from scientific literature using our materials-specific language model (MatSciBERT) and natural language processing techniques. We showcase practical applications including the development of radiation-resistant nuclear waste glasses, scratch-resistant display glasses, and specialty glasses for space applications. The talk concludes by highlighting how this integrated approach has led to the discovery of novel glass compositions with superior properties, validated through experimental synthesis and characterization. Our results demonstrate that the synergistic combination of artificial intelligence, computational modeling, and experimental validation can significantly accelerate the glass design process while reducing resource requirements and environmental impact.

papers.title: The Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neural Network or how Deep Artificial Neural Networks could benefit from Data-Driven Homogeneous Chaos Theory
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning have been widely used in various fields of mathematical computing, physical modeling, computational science, communication science, and stochastic analysis. Approaches based on Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANN) are very popular in our days. Depending on the learning task, the exact form of DANNs is determined via their multi-layer architecture, activation functions and the so-called loss function. However, for a majority of deep learning approaches based on DANNs, the kernel structure of neural signal processing remains the same, where the node response is encoded as a linear superposition of neural activity, while the non-linearity is triggered by the activation functions. In the current paper, we suggest to analyze the neural signal processing in DANNs from the point of view of homogeneous chaos theory as known from polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). From the PCE perspective, the (linear) response on each node of a DANN could be seen as a $1^{st}$ degree multi-variate polynomial of single neurons from the previous layer, i.e. linear weighted sum of monomials. From this point of view, the conventional DANN structure relies implicitly (but erroneously) on a Gaussian distribution of neural signals. Additionally, this view revels that by design DANNs do not necessarily fulfill any orthogonality or orthonormality condition for a majority of data-driven applications. Therefore, the prevailing handling of neural signals in DANNs could lead to redundant representation as any neural signal could contain some partial information from other neural signals. To tackle that challenge, we suggest to employ the data-driven generalization of PCE theory known as arbitrary polynomial chaos (aPC) to construct a corresponding multi-variate orthonormal representations on each node of a DANN to obtain Deep arbitrary polynomial chaos neural networks.

literature_themes.theme: Advancements in Neural Network Architectures for Knowledge Extraction and Document Classification
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers explores innovative approaches to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of knowledge extraction from scientific literature and document classification. It highlights the integration of graph neural networks (GNNs), large language models (LLMs), and hybrid neural network architectures to improve semantic understanding and contextual relevance in processing complex data, particularly in biomedical contexts.
literature_themes.limitations: The studies acknowledge challenges such as the computational expense of deep learning models, low interpretability, and issues like hallucination in LLMs. Additionally, existing models may not fully leverage document structure or contextual word importance, indicating room for improvement in model design and application.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies critical gaps in the current methodologies for knowledge extraction and document classification, suggesting that further research could focus on enhancing model interpretability, reducing computational costs, and improving the integration of contextual information in neural architectures.

literature_themes.theme: Integrating Machine Learning and Simulations for Glass Design
literature_themes.summary: This cluster focuses on a novel framework that combines machine learning, atomistic simulations, and experimental methods to enhance the design and optimization of glass materials. It highlights the use of large-scale machine learning models for predicting glass properties and refining these predictions through advanced neural networks, ultimately facilitating the development of specialized glass compositions for various applications.
literature_themes.limitations: The reliance on extensive experimental databases may limit the applicability of the framework to specific types of glasses. Additionally, the complexity of atomic-scale interactions may pose challenges in fully capturing all relevant properties, and the integration of automated knowledge extraction may not cover all existing literature comprehensively.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies gaps in traditional glass design methodologies by showcasing the potential of machine learning and simulations to accelerate material discovery. It provides a pathway for future research to explore underrepresented glass compositions and optimize properties that have not been extensively studied.

summary: The literature on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge discovery in scientific literature reveals significant advancements in hybrid neural architectures that enhance knowledge extraction and document classification, particularly in biomedical contexts. However, challenges such as computational costs, low interpretability, and limited applicability across domains persist. Additionally, the integration of machine learning with simulations in material design showcases potential methodologies that could be adapted for improved knowledge discovery in literature, highlighting the need for empirical validation and exploration of underrepresented areas.
scholarly_positioning: While prior research has made significant strides in utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge extraction and document classification, particularly in biomedical contexts, these approaches often grapple with high computational costs and low interpretability. Existing methodologies, such as hybrid architectures combining GNNs with large language models, have demonstrated effectiveness but remain largely domain-specific, leaving a gap in applicability across diverse scientific fields. Furthermore, the integration of contextual information and document structure in GNNs has not been adequately addressed, indicating a need for innovative designs that enhance model performance. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by empirically validating GNN applications for large-scale knowledge discovery in scientific literature, thereby contributing to a broader discourse on improving knowledge extraction methodologies.
research_scope: This study will empirically evaluate the effectiveness of a hybrid architecture combining Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and large language models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction from scientific literature across multiple domains, with a focus on biomedical and materials science literature. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the model's performance will be compared against traditional document classification methods using a baseline of existing GNN architectures. Primary outcomes will include accuracy and interpretability of knowledge extraction, measured through metrics such as F1 score and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR). Secondary outcomes will assess computational efficiency and the model's ability to integrate contextual information from document structures, aiming to enhance the overall performance of knowledge discovery methodologies.
concept_definition:
The following table defines key technical concepts operationally: 
- Graph Neural Networks (GNNs): A type of neural network designed to process data structured as graphs, enabling the extraction of relationships and features from nodes and edges in scientific literature. 
- Large Language Models (LLMs): Advanced neural networks trained on extensive text data to understand and generate human-like text, used here for contextual understanding in literature. 
- Hybrid Architecture: A model combining GNNs and LLMs to leverage the strengths of both for improved knowledge extraction. 
- Empirical Validation: The process of testing the model's effectiveness through experiments and real-world data comparison. 
- Interpretability: The degree to which a model's predictions can be understood by humans, assessed through methods like attention visualization and probing. 
- Contextual Integration: The model's ability to utilize structural information from documents to enhance understanding and classification accuracy. 
- F1 Score: A metric that combines precision and recall to evaluate model performance, particularly in classification tasks. 
- Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR): A statistical measure used to evaluate the effectiveness of a model in retrieving relevant information. 
- Hierarchical Attention Mechanisms: Techniques that allow the model to focus on different levels of information (e.g., words, sentences) in a structured manner, improving interpretability and accuracy. 
- Safety Outcomes: Metrics assessing the model's reliability, including unsafe response rate and harmful compliance. 
- User Trust: The confidence users have in the model's predictions, measured through trust calibration and perceived transparency.
technical_feasibility: The proposed study requires access to open-source models for GNNs and LLMs to facilitate hidden state extraction and integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms. It will also need labeled datasets for training and evaluation, as well as GPU resources for model training and experimentation. If user trust is to be assessed, a human-subject design is necessary, including trust calibration measures. Additionally, the study may benefit from multilingual prompt sets and native-speaker validation for broader applicability. To address potential limitations, the design could focus on using available API models for output-level evaluation instead of internal representations, thereby simplifying the resource requirements.

question: How does the integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms within Graph Neural Networks improve document classification accuracy and interpretability in knowledge extraction from scientific literature compared to traditional GNN architectures?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms (independent variable) within Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to enhance document classification accuracy and interpretability (dependent variable) in knowledge extraction from scientific literature. The hierarchical attention mechanisms serve as a mediator by allowing the model to focus on different levels of information, improving the representation of contextual features. This process is moderated by the hybrid architecture that combines GNNs with large language models (LLMs), which provides a richer contextual understanding. The theoretical framework is grounded in the principles of attention mechanisms in neural networks, which suggest that better focus on relevant information leads to improved outcomes. System-level outcomes, such as classification accuracy and interpretability, are influenced by the technical mechanisms of representation features and contextual integration. User-level outcomes, including trust and satisfaction, are mediated by perceived transparency and calibrated trust in the model's predictions. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of hierarchical attention in diverse domains and the impact of contextual integration on user trust and model performance.
hypothesis: Integrating hierarchical attention mechanisms within Graph Neural Networks will significantly enhance document classification accuracy and interpretability in knowledge extraction from scientific literature compared to traditional GNN architectures.

phd_contribution_design: This research proposes the integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms within Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to enhance document classification accuracy and interpretability in knowledge extraction from scientific literature. The mechanism-level claim is that hierarchical attention allows the model to focus on relevant contextual features, which is expected to improve knowledge extraction outcomes compared to traditional GNN architectures. Existing literature fails to adequately address the incorporation of document structure and contextual information in GNNs, highlighting a significant gap in understanding how these elements affect model performance. The falsifiable claim is that the proposed hybrid architecture will yield a statistically significant improvement in F1 Score and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) compared to baseline GNN models. The strongest baseline for comparison will be a conventional GNN architecture without hierarchical attention. Evidence supporting the claim will be derived from empirical evaluations demonstrating enhanced performance metrics. A negative or null result would suggest that hierarchical attention does not contribute to improved knowledge extraction, potentially indicating the need for alternative approaches or further investigation into model design.

proposal: This research proposal aims to investigate the integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms within Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to enhance document classification accuracy and interpretability in knowledge extraction from scientific literature, particularly within the biomedical and materials science domains. Key concepts include GNNs, which process graph-structured data, and Large Language Models (LLMs) that provide contextual understanding. The study is technically feasible, leveraging open-source models such as PyTorch Geometric and labeled datasets from public repositories, with a six-month evaluation period to assess performance against traditional GNN architectures using metrics such as F1 Score and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR). Scholarly positioning highlights the need for improved interpretability and applicability of GNNs across diverse scientific fields, addressing gaps in existing literature regarding the integration of contextual information and document structure. The research question posits how hierarchical attention mechanisms improve document classification accuracy and interpretability compared to traditional GNN architectures. The theoretical mechanism suggests that enhanced focus on contextual features through hierarchical attention mediates improved outcomes, with system-level pathways influencing accuracy and interpretability, while user-level pathways involve trust and satisfaction. The falsifiable hypothesis states that the proposed hybrid architecture will yield statistically significant improvements in F1 Score and MRR compared to baseline GNN models without hierarchical attention. Constructs will be operationalized through defined measurements, including hierarchical attention (IV) assessed via model architecture performance, GNNs (moderator) through baseline comparisons, document classification accuracy (DV) measured by F1 Score, interpretability (DV) evaluated through attention visualization, and user trust (user-level variable) gauged via trust calibration surveys. The methodology involves a comparative study with robust controls, focusing on empirical validation of the hybrid architecture's effectiveness against a conventional GNN baseline. The expected contributions include theoretical advancements in GNN methodologies, technical innovations in hybrid architectures, empirical findings on model performance, and practical deployment guidelines for real-world applications. Key limitations involve potential data sparsity, model interpretability challenges, and the need for user engagement in trust calibration, which will be addressed through comprehensive risk mitigation strategies.
